title: ExpressRoute and VPN Gateway: the road in from the datacentre

videos.script: A company has its own building, with its own network. Sooner or later, that network has to reach Azure. {{office}} There are two roads. The first is a VPN: an encrypted tunnel, across the public internet. {{vpn}} It is cheap, and it is ready in an afternoon. It is also only as steady as the internet is that day. {{internet}} The second is ExpressRoute: a private circuit a carrier builds between your network and Microsoft's. {{circuit}} It never touches the internet. It takes weeks to order, and it is billed every month. {{weeks}} Both roads end in the same place in Azure: a subnet that must be called GatewaySubnet. {{subnet}} You will write the VPN in Bicep, and watch the compiler object to a password written into the file. {{bicep}} Then you will see why one road is never enough, and how companies keep a second one ready. {{end}}
